audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 are marked Skill while the why under that row describes an uncontested proxy phase where 'his Q wall finds nothing to hit'. The full layer also calls a 60.58% matchup EVEN at 6/10 difficulty with the amber tone.
audit.why: 60.58% is the largest edge in this champion's whole table and the prose agrees — the proxy window is free, not a coin flip. Only level 1 and the All Out spike are genuinely contested.
audit.corrected: Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed / Skill / Singed / Singed, and FAV at 4/10 with the favoured tone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells you three times to track All Out's cooldown and never gives it.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80 — a 2-minute gap at rank 1. That is the whole mid-game plan made concrete. It also heals him, which Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds directly answers, and the page never connects those two facts.
audit.corrected: All Out 120/100/80; press Insanity Potion into it so Poison Trail applies Grievous Wounds against the ult's healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's decisive interaction is absent: K'Sante has three dashes — Path Maker (W), Footwork (E) and All Out (R) — and Mega Adhesive grounds every one of them.
audit.why: Riot Mega Adhesive: 'slowing and grounding enemies who walk on it.' Riot Path Maker: 'K'Sante charges up... then dashes.' Riot Footwork: 'K'Sante dashes and gains a shield.' Riot All Out: 'K'Sante knocks an enemy back... Then K'Sante goes All Out and dashes after them.' A champion whose escape, engage and ultimate are all dashes loses all three inside one puddle. Nothing on the page says so, which is why a 60.58% matchup reads as a coin flip.
audit.corrected: Glue first. A K'Sante standing in Mega Adhesive cannot Path Maker, Footwork or All Out.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three ability descriptions are wrong. Ntofo Strikes is written as 'NtNt Q' twice and described as a 'Q wall' and a 'Q knockup'; Path Maker is described as a 'W block' that absorbs your Fling.
audit.why: Riot Ntofo Strikes: 'strikes, damaging and slowing enemies in a short line... At 2 stacks, K'Sante fires a shockwave that pulls enemies in' — a pull, not a wall and not a knockup, 3.5s cooldown. Riot Path Maker: 'charges up, taking reduced damage, then dashes, knocking back and stunning enemies' — damage reduction during the charge, not a block, and it deals true damage, so armour is the wrong answer to it. The shield in his kit is Footwork (E), 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s.
audit.corrected: Ntofo Strikes pulls at two stacks; Path Maker is a charged true-damage dash; Footwork is the shield.

edits.before: At level 1 K'Sante's NtNt Q is slow to stack and his base damage is mediocre — but so is your Poison Trail tickle with no AP, so do not walk at him. Drop Poison Trail through the wave and establish your proxy path instead. The real opening arrives at level 2: the moment he steps up to auto-harass or probe with a stacked Q, W-glue the tile directly behind you, E-fling him into the cloud, and keep moving. He cannot chase you through Mega Adhesive without eating poison and ending up farther from his tower, which inverts his whole early game. Level 3 adds nothing threatening to his kit that changes this pattern — your Fling and glue combo already answers his melee aggression before his W dash can reposition him to safety.
edits.after: At level 1 K'Sante's Ntofo Strikes needs two stacks before the shockwave pulls and his base damage is mediocre — but so is your Poison Trail with no AP, so do not walk at him. Seed the wave and set your proxy path instead. The real opening arrives at level 2: the moment he steps up or loads a second Q stack, W-glue the tile directly behind you, E-fling him into the cloud, and keep moving. Mega Adhesive grounds, and every mobility tool he owns is a dash — inside the goo he cannot Path Maker, cannot Footwork and cannot All Out. Level 3 changes nothing about that pattern; the glue answers his aggression before Path Maker can reposition him to safety.

edits.before: His All Out (R) strips his own resistances and turns him into a mobile fighter — the moment he pops it, disengage through Mega Adhesive and let him chase into full-length poison rather than fighting his duelist form.
edits.after: All Out (R) is 120/100/80 and turns him into a mobile fighter that heals — answer it with Insanity Potion, whose Grievous Wounds cuts that healing, then glue the ground and let him chase the full cloud.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your map window: ghost toward his wave behind his tower, seed Poison Trail through it, and retreat. K'Sante's Q cannot punish what it cannot reach, and his W dash is a short repositioning tool, not a gap-closer capable of catching a ghosting Singed across a full wave. Level 6 is closer — his All Out gives him a fighter mode with real mobility, but your Insanity Potion dumps enough armor, MR, HP regen, and move speed that you can keep running through him rather than away from him. Track his R cooldown the same way you track any ult: when All Out is on cooldown, run straight at him and force the Poison Trail chase; when it comes back up, glue the ground between you and disengage.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your map window: ghost toward his wave behind his tower, seed Poison Trail through it, and retreat. Ntofo Strikes cannot punish what it cannot reach, and Path Maker is a 600-range reposition on 14/13/12/11/10s, not a gap-closer that catches a ghosting Singed across a full wave. Level 6 is closer — All Out gives him a fighter mode with real mobility and healing, but Insanity Potion dumps enough armour, MR, regen and move speed to keep running through him rather than away, and its Grievous Wounds cuts the ult's heal on top. All Out is 120/100/80: a full two minutes at rank 1. Inside that gap, run straight at him and force the poison chase. When it comes back up, glue the ground between you and leave.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track All Out and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 4/10. Mega Adhesive grounds all three of his dashes; only your own discipline loses this.
